audit_result.proof_trace: The SQL function contains zero rate limiting logic — it unconditionally inserts an attendance record on every invocation with no time-window check, count guard, or advisory lock. The function is callable by the `anon` role (GRANT EXECUTE confirmed in 20260317000001_fix_security_permissions.sql L102) and the Supabase anon key is public in the browser bundle, so no authentication barrier prevents unlimited calls. No rate limiting exists at any other layer: no Supabase Edge Functions, no Next.js middleware intercept for RPC calls, and only a client-side processing-state guard that is trivially bypassed by calling PostgREST directly.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker extracts NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL from the browser bundle, then calls POST <supabase-url>/rest/v1/rpc/record_attendance_by_card with a known card_id (NFC Felica UIDs are readable by any NFC reader) in a tight loop, inserting unlimited alternating in/out attendance records and corrupting the attendance history for targeted users.

PROP-kintai-v3-st-pre-006.text: record_attendance_by_card RPC must enforce rate limiting per card_id.
PROP-kintai-v3-st-pre-006.assertion: forall card_id, window: count(record_attendance(card_id, window)) <= RATE_LIMIT
